name: Frozen granular buffer as a playable 'wavetable' voice: capture an evolving sound, freeze, scan time position, sequence pitch via v/oct for overlapping grain polyphony, random-modulate time/size
goal: Turn a granular processor's freeze into an instrument: capture an evolving sound into the buffer (lower-quality mode for ~10 s stereo / 20 s mono), freeze it, trigger seeds from gates, scan the time/position control through the capture like a homemade wavetable, sequence the frozen audio's pitch via v/oct so overlapping grains create a polyphonic illusion, use built-in random modulators on time and grain size, triangle grain window, reverb/delay, and for dark textures pitch the frozen capture down with high density and heavy reverb — the delta vs our granular-stack-freeze skill is pitched, sequenced playback of the frozen buffer.

source.title: Mutable Instruments Beads FREEZE Explained – Frozen Textures & Tricks

prerequisites: Granular processor with freeze, time/position, size, shape, density, pitch (v/oct) input and seed/trigger input

outputs.name: frozen_voice
outputs.description: Pitched, scannable frozen-buffer voice or dark texture

constraints: Original synthesis recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any hybrid synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks or samples copied.
Freeze captures the source at that moment; record what you want to play first.
Values (buffer times per quality mode) are from the presenter's module; other engines differ.

steps.action: Run the granular processor fully wet; generate grains with the seed control; set mid size and a triangle grain shape (fades in and out cleanly); add reverb — integral to big ambient textures.
steps.expect: Smooth grain stream from the input

steps.action: Patch a gate into the seed input and adjust density (grains per seed — it can reach audio rate).
steps.expect: Gated grain bursts of controllable density

steps.action: Select a lower-quality buffer mode to get more record time (presenter: ~10 s stereo / 20 s mono), play an evolving sound in, and freeze it.
Scan the time/position control through the frozen audio — like creating your own wavetable.
steps.expect: Distinct timbres at different scan positions

steps.action: Patch a pitch sequence into v/oct so the frozen buffer is played melodically; use the internal random modulators (attenurandomizers) on time and size; add reverb and delay. Overlapping grains give a polyphony-like overlap.

Dark texture variant: capture a simple tone, pitch the frozen buffer down with density high and reverb high, keep slow random modulation on time so it scrolls and occasionally surfaces higher partials ('ominous wind chimes'); play root changes from a sequencer.
steps.expect: Mostly droning dystopian bed with occasional high glints

steps.action: Optional: modulate freeze itself with gates to alternate between live grains and long held frozen notes.

verification: Changing v/oct changes the pitch of the frozen material without changing the buffer.
Pitch-down + high density yields a continuous drone, not discrete grains.
